newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila wants clearer Spratlys conduct code.
newsitem.headline: Manila wants clearer Spratlys conduct code.

text.p: The Philippines on Monday called for a clearer code of conduct in the disputed South China Sea's Spratly islands to prevent diplomatic clashes between rival claimants.
Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said Manila would seek clearer guidelines at this month's meeting of senior officials of the Association of South East Asian Nations Regional Forum (ARF) in Malaysia.
The Philippines would also raise the issue in regular bilateral talks with China scheduled for May 26-28, Siazon said.
Manila last week accused China of deploying armed naval ships near two islands it claims in the Spratlys, a cluster of tiny islands and reefs with potentially rich oil and gas reserves.
Beijing claims all the islands. The islands are also claimed wholly or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
China said the ships were conducting marine survey measurements and had returned to China.
The Philippines has separately agreed on a code of conduct with China and Vietnam requiring each other not to make any move that would disrupt peace in the Spratlys.
"We have to keep talking to identify more clear guidelines to implement the code of conduct so that we don't have any misunderstanding," Siazon told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
"The basic rule is there is no surprises," he said.

ARF was launched in 1992 allowing ASEAN to discuss security issues with the United States, European Union, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Laos, Cambodia and Papua New Guinea.
ASEAN groups Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei and Singapore.
